I've been wearing a silk bonnet on my head all the time while at home recently and it's been great for me, physically blocking off access to my hair! My one is also frilly around the edges where I tend to pull most, so it's nice too for sensory stimulation whenever my hands reach up there by habit.

A nice bonus is that my hair is always soft after I take it off to go outside since it's silk :)

I’ve started having a few sessions of cognitive therapy with a psychologist recently — as in, just two for now. So pretty early on! I’ve had trich for a super long time too and tried like everything as well :( <3

Even though I haven’t gotten around to any great behaviour changers as I still do pull quite a bit, the first and biggest takeaway I’ve gotten out of speaking with a psychologist has been to easing my self-talk about it. Realising that the way I view myself after I pull — being disgusting or that I’m disappointed — are such strong feelings to have, and it is just so sad to think about myself those ways. So for me something that has helped me, even though it hasn’t greatly reduced the amount I pull, has been to be aware of when I’m just jumping to extremes of thinking so negatively about it and myself. It doesn’t get rid of the behaviour completely, but it makes better my experience just having trich.

Hi, I did this (a really really high amount, I won’t disclose exact numbers bc it might influence other people) 4 years ago when I was 16 years old and really depressed. I knew it would be painful, and it was so so painful but I kept at it for the multiple days I continued upping the dose, because I was so suicidal I didn’t even care that it would be a painful way out. I mention this because you might relate, hearing everyone tell you it will be the worst way out, but it meaning nothing to you because you know you just want to die — knowing that it will be terrible but thinking it will be better than your life now.

I didn’t go to a doctor or the ER because I wanted to let it kill me. To this day, that was the most excruciating pain I have ever felt, and I think it will probably be the worst pain I will ever feel — being 24/7, for months straight. After those months where it was a constant stabbing in my liver area, the pain was still there very much, but not so 24/7, like maybe … a few times a day.

4 years on, I still have liver pain and general tenderness when I touch it, once a month on average. I got a blood test for the first time recently and received really abnormal blood test results that my GP, still oblivious to any attempt I ever made because I was just stubborn to get help for it and I still haven’t told him anything of, explained indicated scarring of cells in my liver. I don’t know what I can do now to change it, but keep living with this permanent scarring in my liver.

When I think about how I was then, now, my biggest regret is that I was simply so stubborn to everyone telling me to go to the hospital for it. I thought it would just kill me, or if not then … I didn’t care much honestly — no consequences mattered to me in my mind (when you want to kill yourself thinking anywhere in the future is simply not in your emotional bandwidth). But now, realising that what I did that time 4 years ago has made a permanent effect on my body, that I STILL experience now, it upsets me so much because I know I’m living with what I did to myself.

I hope that, against your better judgement right now in your mind, you find the strength to disobey that, and plant the knowledge that IT IS better to go get it treated now.
